business_summary.text: AWL Agri Business Limited is a diversified Food and FMCG company, with Edible Oil as its foundation and growing packaged Food, future-ready channels, and value-added businesses.

call_points.text: Food & FMCG revenue growth guided at 18-20% for the rest of FY27.
Edible Oil volume growth guided at 5-6% for the rest of FY27.
Food & FMCG EBITDA margin of 6% in Q1 is an average, not a new guidance target.
No specific hedging proportion disclosed; brand strength cited as the primary hedge.
Edible oil prices rose about 10% in March and were passed on to consumers.
Kohinoor clocked over 50,000 tonnes in FY26, up about 20%.
New Krishnapatnam oleo-chemical installation expected to add volume from early Q1FY27.
Trade credit and borrowings shift between lines; current assets comfortably cover current liabilities.
Every ₹10 move in edible oil prices moves demand about 1%, per management.
No plan to enter palm plantation; promoter Wilmar already has plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia.

guidance.statement: Food volumes to grow in double digit, at least mid-teens, in FY27 with top line prioritised over margin
Food to remain EBITDA-neutral till FY27, then build ₹1,500-2,000 per tonne EBITDA from FY28
Alternate channel to reach 30-35% of volumes from 15% today

industry: Fast Moving Consumer Goods > Agricultural Food & other Products > Edible Oil

operating_notes.text: Edible oil prices in March: sunflower above $1,400 a tonne, soya near $1,300 and palm $1,220-1,250.
Alternate channel is 15% of edible oil volume and 25% of food volume, growing 43% in Q4FY26.
Oleo chemical is 30% of Industry Essentials and specialty chemicals 7-8% of that portfolio.
Edible Oil raw material stock days: 30-35 days.
Edible Oil regional mix: 30% palm, 30-35% soya, 20% sunflower, 15% local oils (mustard, groundnuts, cotton, rice bran).
Food business B2C mix: 80%, B2B mix: 20%.

timeline.summary: AWL Agri Business Limited held its Q1FY27 earnings call on July 30, 2026, reporting strong revenue and profit growth.

watchlist.response: Management said it cannot quantify and depends on market opportunity; base case is mid-teens volume growth.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the volume level at which food margins hold if volumes are prioritised over margin.

watchlist.response: COO gave a demand rule of thumb (1% demand change per ₹10) and described inventory management, but no margin sensitivity figure.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for sensitivity of margins to ₹5-10 moves in edible oil prices.

watchlist.response: Management attributed it to standalone versus consolidated and G2G normalisation.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked why the press release food volume growth (about 1%) diverged from the reported 6%.

watchlist.response: Management provided a steady-state assumption of ₹700 Cr per year but did not give a specific plan, stating capacities will be added as needed.
watchlist.text: What is the specific CAPEX plan for the next four years?

watchlist.response: Management did not provide a specific proportion, stating that brand strength is their primary hedge and they do not speculate.
watchlist.text: What is the proportion of raw materials hedged vs. kept open?
